newsitem.title: GREECE: Short-end of Greek yield curve firms on FRN moves.
newsitem.headline: Short-end of Greek yield curve firms on FRN moves.

text.p: Greek depo rates and forex forwards for periods up to six months were firmer with the shortest periods in the lead as players positioned themselves ahead of the FRN auction on October 21, dealers said.
"The yield curve up to six months has shifted upwards on FRN positioning," said a trader at a foreign bank. "The rise is more accentuated in the very short end of the yield curve."
The trader said the surplus liquidity was forex-linked and therefore more sensitive to interest rate and forex moves than deposits, making banks more cautious.
"We do not really know the exact amount of surplus liquidity in the system," he said. "This increases uncertainty ahead of the auction."
Traders put surplus liquidity above 100 billion drachmas.
Greece will auction 250 billion drachmas of seven-year floaters with the first coupon set at 14 percent on Monday, October 21, the finance ministry said in a statement today.
The spread is held constant at 150 basis points but the benchmark 12-month T-bill is slashed by 20 basis points to 12.50 percent.

The treasury reserves the right to accept non-competitive bids up to 30 percent of the auctioned amount, it said. It also reserves the right not to accept all or some of the competitive bids to be submitted, the statement said.
It also reserves the right to accept competitive bids over the 250 billion drachma amount if non-competitive bids do not suffice to cover the 30 percent allotment.
"There was demand for bonds due 2002 and 2003 up to the announcement of the the FRN auction," said a bond trader at a foreign bank.
Another senior trader said he expected the average FRN around par inclusive of commissions.
The mark was quoted at 156.32/42 drachmas from Wednesday's 156.405 fix, the dollar at 240.94/99 drachmas from 240.930 and the Ecu at 300.09/19 from 300.210 drachmas.
"I estimate today's gross outflows at 100 million ecus," said a forex trader. "The drachma started strong against the ecu but softened later on profit taking."
